proposal.utterance: What BFO category best fits 'the normative force of an obligation'?

entities.label: NormativeForce
entities.rationale: Normative force is the capacity of an obligation to bind a bearer to compliance, to generate reasons for action, and to ground enforcement. This capacity is internally grounded in the obligation itself (or in the legal/moral structure that constitutes the obligation) and is directed toward realization in compliant or non-compliant behavior. That profile fits BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016): a specifically dependent continuant that is internally grounded in the structure of its bearer and tends toward realization in a process. It is not merely a static quality (BFO_0000019) because it carries a directedness toward realization; it is not a Role (BFO_0000023) because it is not externally conferred social status but an intrinsic normative property of the obligation token. A sub-class of Disposition under the existing LegalObligation role class is the cleanest fit.

relations.rationale: NormativeForce is a kind of Disposition: internally grounded in its bearer (a legal obligation token) and realizable in a process of compliance or enforcement.
As a Disposition, NormativeForce is a specifically dependent continuant (BFO_0000020), inhering in exactly one bearer (the obligation token).

open_questions: Should NormativeForce inhere specifically in instances of working:LegalObligation, or is it intended more broadly to cover moral obligations and other deontic statuses as well?

Do you want to distinguish the force as a disposition of the obligation itself (inhering in a GDC token) versus a disposition of the person who bears the obligation (inhering in the agent)? BFO requires exactly one bearer, so this choice affects the domain of RO_0000052.

Is 'normative force' intended to be a quality (a stable magnitude, e.g. degree of bindingness) rather than a disposition (a directed capacity)? If strength/degree is the primary concern, BFO_0000019 Quality might be preferred instead.
proposal.rationale_summary: The normative force of an obligation is best typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016). A disposition is a specifically dependent continuant that is grounded in the intrinsic structure of its bearer and is oriented toward realization in some process. Normative force fits this profile: it inheres in the obligation token, it is grounded in the legal or moral structure that constitutes that obligation, and it is directed toward realization in processes of compliance, enforcement, or sanction. This distinguishes it from a mere Quality (which would capture a static measurable property without directedness) and from a Role (which is externally grounded in social recognition rather than in the obligation's own constitution). The new class NormativeForce is therefore proposed as a subclass of BFO Disposition, with the expectation that individual instances of NormativeForce inhere in (RO_0000052) individual obligation tokens, instances of working:LegalObligation.
